cycling.notes: Cycling cadence is 90 rpm and must stay 90: the halving correction applies to running sports only.

gaps.notes: Two 100 second holes. The interval after a sample belongs to that sample, so a hole that follows a running sample is charged to running time.
gaps.watch: records every second, but the watch was paused twice

hilly.notes: Climbs 60 m then descends 60 m; the elevation stream follows the running samples.

hr_gps_run.notes: GPS present, heart rate present, cadence stored halved (80 -> 160 spm).

low_resolution.notes: Five-second sampling: intervals are five seconds wide, not one.

mixed_run.notes: Walk warm-up, run, 20 s stand, run. Stored cadence is halved.

no_cadence.notes: No cadence field anywhere: every cadence metric must be null, never zero.
no_cadence.watch: records every second, no cadence sensor

real_garmin_gap.notes: The same real-watch format as real_garmin_run, with the 204 second hole the real files contain: the watch records nothing for three and a half minutes and the distance does not advance across it. The interval after a sample belongs to that sample, so the hole is charged to the running, while the laps — which only count the intervals between two running samples — are not.
real_garmin_gap.watch: records irregularly, with a 204 second hole

real_garmin_nulls.notes: The real-watch format, with the reserved 'no value' sentinels in the fields the importer reads: the classic speed and altitude are 0xFFFF in the first half of the file and the enhanced pair is 0xFFFFFFFF in the second, the heart rate and the cadence are 0xFF, one distance is 0xFFFFFFFF and one position is 0x7FFFFFFF, and the file's serial number is the uint32z null of 0. That is the sentinel of every base type the importer reads a field of: uint8, uint16, uint32, sint32 and uint32z. The sint, 64-bit and float sentinels are not in the file because the importer reads no field of those types. A sentinel is an absent field, and it is absent before any range check: 0xFFFF as a speed is 65.535 m/s, which is inside the range and would pass every check, and 0xFF as a heart rate is 255 bpm, which is inside 0-300. Twelve laps, as the real files have. Note the external id: the reference reads a null serial number as the field wrapper rather than as an absent field, so the id is the literal string 'serial_number: None'. That is the reference's behaviour today and it looks like a bug in value_of; the golden freezes it as it is.
real_garmin_nulls.watch: records irregularly, with a block of absent values

real_garmin_run.notes: The byte format of a real Garmin Forerunner 965 file (thirteen of them, March 2025 to October 2026): FIT protocol 1.0, enhanced speed and altitude instead of speed and altitude, fields and messages the published FIT profile does not describe, a redefined local message number and an irregular record stream. The format came from a real watch; the data did not, and every position is fabricated.
real_garmin_run.watch: records irregularly, one to fourteen seconds apart

short_effort.notes: One lap only: thirds are empty, so drift and CV metrics are null.

treadmill.notes: Treadmill: no position fields at all. The FIT session sport is 'running'; the reference importer ignores sub_sport, so a treadmill run is 'running'.
